question:
Let $S = \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}$. Consider the relation $R$ on $S$ defined by: $a R b$ if $ab > 0$.

(a) Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation on $S$.

(b) Find the equivalence classes.

(c) How does this partition $S$? Give explicit sets.
explanation:
(a) Reflexivity: $a R a$ iff $a^2 > 0$, which is true for all $a \neq 0$. So $R$ is reflexive.

Symmetry: If $a R b$, then $ab > 0$, so $ba > 0$, i.e., $b R a$.

Transitivity: If $a R b$ ($ab > 0$) and $b R c$ ($bc > 0$), then $b > 0$ or $b < 0$.

Case 1: $b > 0$. Then $a > 0$ and $c > 0$, so $ac > 0$.

Case 2: $b < 0$. Then $a < 0$ and $c < 0$, so $ac > 0$.

Thus, in either case, $a R c$.

(b) The equivalence class of $1$ is $\{x \in S : x > 0\}$ (the positive reals).

The equivalence class of $-1$ is $\{x \in S : x < 0\}$ (the negative reals).

(c) Thus, $S$ is partitioned into the set of positive real numbers and the set of negative real numbers.

options.A:
(a) $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so it is an equivalence relation.
(b) The equivalence classes are $(0,\infty)$ and $(-\infty,0)$.
(c) $S$ is partitioned as $S=(0,\infty)\cup(-\infty,0)$ with the two classes disjoint.
options.B:
(a) $R$ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive.
(b) The equivalence classes are singleton sets.
(c) $S$ has no partition.
options.C:
(a) $R$ is not reflexive because $a^2<0$.
(b) The equivalence class of every element is empty.
(c) $S$ is partitioned into rational and irrational numbers.
options.D:
(a) $R$ is symmetric only.
(b) The only equivalence class is $S$.
(c) $S$ is not partitioned.
